sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Imagine for a moment the year 1800.
sentences.zh: 试想一下1800年的情景。

sentences.en: A doctor is meeting with a patient,
sentences.zh: 一位医生正在会诊病人，

sentences.en: most likely in the patient's home.
sentences.zh: 很可能是在病人的家中。

sentences.en: The patient is complaining about shortness of breath,
sentences.zh: 病人抱怨呼吸短促、

sentences.en: a cough, a fever.
sentences.zh: 咳嗽、发烧。

sentences.en: The doctor listens to the patient's complaints,
sentences.zh: 医生听取病人的主诉，

sentences.en: asks a ton of questions, scribbles some notes.
sentences.zh: 问了一大堆问题，草草记下笔记。

sentences.en: Producer Emmett Fitzgerald.
sentences.zh: 制片人埃米特·菲茨杰拉德。

sentences.en: And the doctor might check the patient's pulse.
sentences.zh: 医生可能还会检查病人的脉搏。

sentences.en: But unlike today, what's happening inside of the
sentences.zh: 但与今天不同的是，病人身体内部发生的情况

sentences.en: patient is basically unknowable.
sentences.zh: 基本上是无法知晓的。

sentences.en: There's no MRI, no x-rays.
sentences.zh: 没有核磁共振，没有X光。

sentences.en: The living body is like a black box
sentences.zh: 活体就像一个无法打开的

sentences.en: that can't be opened.
sentences.zh: 黑匣子。

sentences.en: The only way for a doctor to figure out what's wrong with a patient is to ask
sentences.zh: 医生找出病人病因的唯一方法就是询问

sentences.en: them.
sentences.zh: 他们。

sentences.en: You needed the patient to tell you what was wrong and what they were suffering.
sentences.zh: 你需要病人告诉你哪里不对劲，以及他们正在遭受什么痛苦。

sentences.en: So doctors
sentences.zh: 所以医生们

sentences.en: were very interested in the patient's history, the story of what the symptom was,
sentences.zh: 非常关注病人的病史，即症状的来龙去脉，

sentences.en: how long it had been there, how had it changed, what made it better, what made it worse.
sentences.zh: 症状持续了多久，如何变化，什么情况会好转，什么情况会恶化。

sentences.en: This is Dr. Jacqueline Duffin.
sentences.zh: 这位是杰奎琳·达芬医生。

sentences.en: I am a hematologist and a historian of medicine at Queen's University.
sentences.zh: 我是女王大学的血液学家和医学史学家。

sentences.en: Duffin says that because the patient's story was all the doctor had to go on,
sentences.zh: 达芬说，因为病人的叙述是医生唯一的依据，

sentences.en: the symptoms were often seen as diseases in themselves.
sentences.zh: 症状往往被视为疾病本身。

sentences.en: So for example, today, if you have a fever, you think of it as a symptom of some underlying disease
sentences.zh: 例如，今天如果你发烧，你会认为这是某种潜在疾病的症状，

sentences.en: like the flu.
sentences.zh: 比如流感。

sentences.en: But back at the turn of the 19th century, the fever itself was considered the
sentences.zh: 但在19世纪之交，发烧本身就被认为是

sentences.en: disease.
sentences.zh: 疾病。

sentences.en: There were all different kinds of fevers and fever itself was a broad category of diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 当时有各种各样的发烧，发烧本身就是一个广泛的诊断类别。

sentences.en: Because doctors had no way of connecting symptoms with what was actually going on inside the body.
sentences.zh: 因为医生无法将症状与身体内部实际发生的情况联系起来。

sentences.en: Until someone built a device that would help the doctor open the black box and travel inside the
sentences.zh: 直到有人制造出一种设备，可以帮助医生打开这个黑匣子，深入

sentences.en: human body.
sentences.zh: 人体内部。

sentences.en: And suddenly the doctor could hear everything so much more clearly.
sentences.zh: 突然间，医生能听得如此清晰。

sentences.en: The heart,
sentences.zh: 心脏、

sentences.en: the lungs, the breath.
sentences.zh: 肺部、呼吸声。

sentences.en: And everything changed.
sentences.zh: 一切都改变了。

sentences.en: The inventor of the stethoscope was, unsurprisingly, a doctor.
sentences.zh: 听诊器的发明者不出所料，是一位医生。

sentences.en: René Leineck was born in Brittany in 1781.
sentences.zh: 勒内·雷奈克于1781年出生在布列塔尼。

sentences.en: And he went to medical school in Paris, where he learned
sentences.zh: 他在巴黎读医学院，在那里他学会了

sentences.en: to practice percussion, a technique in which the doctor taps their fingers against a patient's chest
sentences.zh: 叩诊，这是一种医生用手指敲击病人胸部，

sentences.en: and listens to the sound to determine things like if fluid is building up in the patient's lungs.
sentences.zh: 通过声音来判断诸如肺部是否有积液等情况的技术。

sentences.en: Leineck uses the technique for years.
sentences.zh: 雷奈克使用这种技术多年。

sentences.en: And in 1816, he's examining a patient and he percusses her torso.
sentences.zh: 1816年，他在检查一名病人时，叩诊了她的躯干。

sentences.en: But she's a little bit plump.
sentences.zh: 但她有点胖。

sentences.en: And because she's plump, he's not getting much sound back from
sentences.zh: 因为她很胖，他从

sentences.en: percussing.
sentences.zh: 叩诊中听不到什么声音。

sentences.en: He thought about putting his ear right against the patient's breast, but he decided that
sentences.zh: 他想过把耳朵直接贴在病人的胸口，但他觉得

sentences.en: that would be inappropriate.
sentences.zh: 那样做不合适。

sentences.en: So he took a notebook that he had with him and he rolled it up into a
sentences.zh: 于是他拿起随身携带的笔记本，把它卷成一个

sentences.en: little cylinder and he put one end on the patient's chest and one end on his ear.
sentences.zh: 小圆筒，一端放在病人的胸口，另一端贴在自己的耳朵上。

sentences.en: And he tells us he
sentences.zh: 他告诉我们，

sentences.en: was struck by how clearly he could hear her heart beating and her breath sounds.
sentences.zh: 他被自己能如此清晰地听到她的心跳和呼吸声所震撼。

sentences.en: I was satisfied to
sentences.zh: 我很高兴能

sentences.en: hear the beating of the heart in a manner that was clearer and more distinct than I had ever heard it
sentences.zh: 听到心跳声，这种方式比我以前通过

sentences.en: by direct application of the ear.
sentences.zh: 直接用耳朵贴听到的声音更清晰、更分明。

sentences.en: He was so impressed by the quality of the sound that he set about trying
sentences.zh: 他对声音的质量印象深刻，于是着手尝试

sentences.en: to construct the perfect device for listening to the internal sounds of the body, all based on that
sentences.zh: 制造一种完美的设备来聆听身体内部的声音，所有这些都基于

sentences.en: same cylinder shape.
sentences.zh: 同样的圆筒形状。

sentences.en: People said that he became a cylindromaniac, a cylinder maniac, because he
sentences.zh: 人们说他成了“圆筒狂人”，因为他

sentences.en: he was convinced that the instrument mediating between the two bodies of the patient and the doctor
sentences.zh: 确信这种介于病人与医生两个身体之间的仪器

sentences.en: improved what the doctor could hear.
sentences.zh: 改善了医生的听诊效果。

sentences.en: He used a lathe to carve cylinders out of wood.
sentences.zh: 他用旋床把木头雕刻成圆筒。

sentences.en: And at first he wanted to call his new device
sentences.zh: 起初他想把他的新设备称为

sentences.en: the cylinder.
sentences.zh: 圆筒。

sentences.en: But eventually he settled on the stethoscope, which means to explore the cheSt.
sentences.zh: 但最终他选择了“听诊器”（stethoscope），意思是探索胸部。

sentences.en: But Leineck's original stethoscope looks pretty different from the ones we're used to today.
sentences.zh: 但雷奈克最初的听诊器看起来和我们今天习惯使用的非常不同。

sentences.en: It's a long tube-like cylinder.
sentences.zh: 它是一个长长的管状圆筒。

sentences.en: It looks like a small handheld telescope.
sentences.zh: 看起来像一个小型的便携式望远镜。

sentences.en: Leineck started using his new invention to listen to the heart sounds and the breathing sounds
sentences.zh: 雷奈克开始使用他的新发明来聆听医院里

sentences.en: of all of the patients in his hospital.
sentences.zh: 所有病人的心跳声和呼吸声。

sentences.en: And he started to invent words to describe the sounds because nobody had heard these sounds before.
sentences.zh: 他开始发明词汇来描述这些声音，因为以前没有人听过这些声音。

sentences.en: Leineck had invented a way to hear the inner workings of the human body.
sentences.zh: 雷奈克发明了一种聆听人体内部运作的方法。

sentences.en: But that wasn't enough by itself.
sentences.zh: 但这本身还不够。

sentences.en: He wanted to connect the sounds he was hearing in his patients
sentences.zh: 他想把他听到的病人声音

sentences.en: with what was actually happening anatomically inside their bodies.
sentences.zh: 与他们体内解剖学上实际发生的情况联系起来。

sentences.en: And how do you connect sounds to what's actually happening inside a body?
sentences.zh: 你如何将声音与身体内部实际发生的情况联系起来呢？

sentences.en: You listen to people right before they die.
sentences.zh: 你在人们临终前听他们（的声音）。

sentences.en: He ran around the ward listening to all the patients, documenting their symptoms,
sentences.zh: 他在病房里跑来跑去，听所有病人的声音，记录他们的症状，

sentences.en: listening to the sounds they made, and then connecting them to the discoveries he would
sentences.zh: 聆听他们发出的声音，然后将这些声音与他去世后

sentences.en: make at their autopsy when they died.
sentences.zh: 尸检时的发现联系起来。

sentences.en: He thought that every abnormal sound he heard with his stethoscope should correspond to an
sentences.zh: 他认为他用听诊器听到的每一个异常声音都应该对应一个

sentences.en: anatomical finding during the autopsy.
sentences.zh: 尸检时的解剖学发现。

sentences.en: So that if you hear this sound, it equals that anatomical finding later.
sentences.zh: 这样，如果你听到这个声音，它就等于以后对应的解剖学发现。

sentences.en: So that the stethoscope was a way of practicing the autopsy before the patient became a cadaver.
sentences.zh: 所以听诊器是一种在病人变成尸体之前进行尸检的方法。

sentences.en: I mean, we're all just future cadavers, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们都是未来的尸体，对吧？

sentences.en: But the stethoscope gave us a way of looking inside of a body before it was dead to see
sentences.zh: 但听诊器给了我们一种在身体死亡前观察内部的方法，以查看

sentences.en: what was causing a particular medical problem.
sentences.zh: 是什么导致了特定的医疗问题。

sentences.en: In a relatively short period of time, Leineck made some key discoveries using his stethoscope.
sentences.zh: 在相对较短的时间内，雷奈克利用他的听诊器做出了一些关键发现。

sentences.en: For example, he figured out that when a person has fluid beneath their lungs,
sentences.zh: 例如，他发现当一个人的肺部下方有积液时，

sentences.en: they make a sound kind of like a goat.
sentences.zh: 他们发出的声音有点像山羊。

sentences.en: A kind of bleeding sound like this.
sentences.zh: 一种像这样的羊叫声。

sentences.en: A sound he called egophony.
sentences.zh: 他称之为“羊鸣音”。

sentences.en: He also discovered sounds that tracked with the different stages of tuberculosis,
sentences.zh: 他还发现了与肺结核不同阶段相对应的声音，

sentences.en: the number one killer in Europe at the time.
sentences.zh: 这是当时欧洲的第一大杀手。

sentences.en: Leineck published his results linking different diagnoses with anatomical changes in the body
sentences.zh: 雷奈克发表了他的研究结果，将不同的诊断与身体内部的解剖学变化联系起来，

sentences.en: that could be detected using his new stethoscope.
sentences.zh: 这些变化可以使用他的新听诊器检测出来。

sentences.en: Doctors who were his colleagues loved it.
sentences.zh: 他的同事医生们非常喜欢它。

sentences.en: They felt that every disease would eventually be attached to an anatomical finding and an anatomical change.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得每一种疾病最终都会与解剖学发现和解剖学变化联系起来。

sentences.en: Some doctors began using Leineck's new device themselves.
sentences.zh: 一些医生开始亲自使用雷奈克的新设备。

sentences.en: He even put a diagram of it in his book so you could make your own quite easily
sentences.zh: 他甚至在他的书中放了一张图表，这样你就可以很容易地自己制作一个，

sentences.en: or have it made for you by any carpenter.
sentences.zh: 或者让任何木匠为你制作。

sentences.en: And as these doctors used the stethoscope to make more important discoveries about the body,
sentences.zh: 随着这些医生使用听诊器对身体做出更重要的发现，

sentences.en: new categories of disease were created.
sentences.zh: 新的疾病类别被创造出来了。

sentences.en: For example, before the stethoscope,
sentences.zh: 例如，在听诊器出现之前，

sentences.en: a lot of different ailments were all lumped into one disease called dyspnea,
sentences.zh: 许多不同的疾病都被归为一种叫做“呼吸困难”的疾病，

sentences.en: which means shortness of breath.
sentences.zh: 意思是呼吸短促。

sentences.en: But after Leineck, shortness of breath became a symptom
sentences.zh: 但在雷奈克之后，呼吸短促成为了

sentences.en: of various heart or lung problems that could be diagnosed using the stethoscope.
sentences.zh: 各种心脏或肺部问题的症状，这些问题可以使用听诊器进行诊断。

sentences.en: Medical language completely changed
sentences.zh: 医学语言完全改变了，

sentences.en: as doctors invented new anatomical words for diseases like bronchitis,
sentences.zh: 因为医生们为支气管炎等疾病发明了新的解剖学词汇，

sentences.en: which means the inflammation of the bronchial tubes,
sentences.zh: 意思是支气管发炎，

sentences.en: the airways that lead to the lungs.
sentences.zh: 即通往肺部的气道。

sentences.en: Little by little, our entire understanding of disease shifted.
sentences.zh: 一点一点地，我们对疾病的整体理解发生了转变。

sentences.en: It became more objective.
sentences.zh: 它变得更加客观。

sentences.en: Diseases went from being constellations of symptoms felt subjectively by the patient
sentences.zh: 疾病从病人主观感受到的症状集合，

sentences.en: to anatomical or chemical alterations inside the body detected by the doctor.
sentences.zh: 变成了医生检测到的身体内部的解剖学或化学改变。

sentences.en: This shift in how people thought about disease changed the relationships between doctors and patients,
sentences.zh: 这种对疾病看法上的转变改变了医生和病人之间的关系，

sentences.en: with the doctors suddenly having a lot more power.
sentences.zh: 医生突然拥有了更大的权力。

sentences.en: So before the stethoscope, to be sick, you had to feel sick.
sentences.zh: 所以在听诊器出现之前，要生病，你必须感觉自己生病了。

sentences.en: After the stethoscope, to be sick, the doctor had to find something.
sentences.zh: 在听诊器出现之后，要生病，医生必须发现点什么。

sentences.en: It didn't matter what the patient thought, what was wrong with them.
sentences.zh: 病人认为自己哪里不对劲并不重要。

sentences.en: It mattered more what the doctor found.
sentences.zh: 医生发现了什么才更重要。

sentences.en: Leineck himself actually worried that many doctors were taking his ideas too far.
sentences.zh: 雷奈克本人实际上担心许多医生把他的想法推得太远了。

sentences.en: He believed that listening to what patients had to say was still important to understanding disease.
sentences.zh: 他认为倾听病人的诉说对于理解疾病仍然很重要。

sentences.en: But the quest for objective information about disease was underway.
sentences.zh: 但对疾病客观信息的追求已经开始了。

sentences.en: And the stethoscope was just the beginning.
sentences.zh: 而听诊器仅仅是个开始。

sentences.en: Then we got x-rays, which do the same thing at the end of the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 后来我们有了X光，在19世纪末也做了同样的事情。

sentences.en: And now we have CT scanners and MRIs and PET scans.
sentences.zh: 现在我们有了CT扫描、核磁共振和PET扫描。

sentences.en: And all of these marvelous devices are basically trading upon the same paradigm that the stethoscope brought along,
sentences.zh: 所有这些奇妙的设备基本上都在沿用听诊器带来的相同范式，

sentences.en: that we should be able somehow to image the pathological anatomical abnormalities inside the body
sentences.zh: 即我们应该能够以某种方式对身体内部的病理学解剖异常进行成像，

sentences.en: to reach the diagnosis, whether the patient has any symptoms at all or not.
sentences.zh: 以得出诊断，无论病人是否有任何症状。

sentences.en: These new technologies have led to so many important discoveries about the human body and disease.
sentences.zh: 这些新技术在人体和疾病方面带来了许多重要的发现。

sentences.en: Today, we can spot tumors before they become life-threatening
sentences.zh: 今天，我们可以在肿瘤危及生命之前发现它们，

sentences.en: and diagnose problems like high blood pressure before it causes heart disease.
sentences.zh: 并在高血压导致心脏病之前诊断出这些问题。

sentences.en: But there are also patients today who struggle because they've got tons of symptoms,
sentences.zh: 但今天也有一些病人因为有大量的症状而挣扎，

sentences.en: but the doctor can't find anything quote-unquote wrong with them.
sentences.zh: 但医生却无法发现他们有什么“所谓的”问题。

sentences.en: The paradigm shift brought on by the stethoscope has pushed doctors and patients further apart.
sentences.zh: 听诊器带来的范式转移使医生和病人之间的距离更远了。

sentences.en: The doctor is no longer visiting you in your bedroom,
sentences.zh: 医生不再去你的卧室探望你，

sentences.en: interviewing you about every tiny detail of your experience.
sentences.zh: 询问你经历的每一个微小细节。

sentences.en: And sometimes patients end up feeling like just a collection of data points rather than a whole human being.
sentences.zh: 有时病人最终感觉自己只是一个数据点的集合，而不是一个完整的人。

sentences.en: Rene Leinek died in 1826 at the age of 45, most likely from tuberculosis,
sentences.zh: 雷内·雷奈克于1826年去世，享年45岁，很可能是死于肺结核，

sentences.en: a disease he and his stethoscope helped us understand.
sentences.zh: 这是一种他和他的听诊器帮助我们了解的疾病。

sentences.en: It's been 200 years since he first rolled up his notebook and pressed it to that patient's cheSt.
sentences.zh: 距离他第一次卷起笔记本并将其按在病人的胸口已经过去200年了。

sentences.en: Medicine looks completely different than it did back then.
sentences.zh: 医学看起来与当时完全不同。

sentences.en: But somehow, the stethoscope has endured.
sentences.zh: 但不知何故，听诊器一直沿用至今。

sentences.en: There are certain tools of the trade that we have gotten rid of.
sentences.zh: 我们已经淘汰了一些行业工具。

sentences.en: So you don't really see doctors carrying around this big black bag.
sentences.zh: 所以你真的看不到医生随身携带那个黑色大包了。

sentences.en: This is Dr. Andrew Bomback.
sentences.zh: 这位是安德鲁·邦巴克医生。

sentences.en: He's a nephrologist, a kidney doctor,
sentences.zh: 他是一位肾脏科医生，也就是肾病专家，

sentences.en: and an assistant professor at the Columbia University College of Physicians and Surgeons.
sentences.zh: 同时也是哥伦比亚大学内外科医学院的助理教授。

sentences.en: Most doctors nowadays don't carry around reflex hammers unless they're, you know, neurologists.
sentences.zh: 如今大多数医生都不会随身携带叩诊锤，除非他们是神经科医生。

sentences.en: Most doctors don't wear that light on their head.
sentences.zh: 大多数医生也不会在头上戴那种头灯。

sentences.en: But the stethoscope has never really fallen out of practice.
sentences.zh: 但听诊器却从未真正退出临床应用。

sentences.en: But of course, doctors aren't walking around with wooden cylinders anymore.
sentences.zh: 当然，医生们现在也不会再随身带着木制圆筒了。

sentences.en: In the 1840s, they began experimenting with flexible tubing.
sentences.zh: 19世纪40年代，他们开始尝试使用软管。

sentences.en: And soon after, an Irish physician invented the binaural stethoscope design
sentences.zh: 不久之后，一位爱尔兰医生发明了双耳听诊器设计，

sentences.en: with two earpieces that we still use.
sentences.zh: 也就是我们至今仍在使用的那种带有两个耳塞的设计。

sentences.en: Today, there are a few kinds of specialized stethoscopes for particular types of listening.
sentences.zh: 如今，针对特定的听诊需求，有几种专门的听诊器。

sentences.en: And more recently, companies have developed electronic stethoscopes
sentences.zh: 最近，一些公司还开发了电子听诊器，

sentences.en: with enhanced sound quality and the ability to record.
sentences.zh: 不仅音质更佳，还具备录音功能。

sentences.en: But to this day, when you walk into a doctor's office for a routine exam,
sentences.zh: 但时至今日，当你走进医生的办公室进行常规检查时，

sentences.en: you can expect to feel the familiar stethoscope sliding along your back.
sentences.zh: 你依然会感到那个熟悉的听诊器在你的背上滑动。

sentences.en: But that could be changing.
sentences.zh: 但这可能正在发生改变。

sentences.en: For almost 200 years, the trusty stethoscope has been at the forefront of the diagnostic procedure,
sentences.zh: 近200年来，可靠的听诊器一直处于诊断流程的最前沿，

sentences.en: constantly hanging around the necks of doctors and often used.
sentences.zh: 它总是挂在医生的脖子上，并被频繁使用。

sentences.en: But new technology is threatening to exile this old friend to the archives of medical history.
sentences.zh: 但新技术正威胁着要将这位老朋友打入医学历史的档案库。

sentences.en: X-rays and ultrasound have given doctors a clearer window into the body than ever before.
sentences.zh: X光和超声波为医生提供了比以往任何时候都更清晰的身体观察窗口。

sentences.en: And with new portable ultrasound machines,
sentences.zh: 有了新型便携式超声波设备，

sentences.en: doctors can see an image of a hole in a patient's heart right from the bedside.
sentences.zh: 医生在床边就能直接看到病人心脏缺损的图像。

sentences.en: The rise of portable ultrasound has some doctors arguing that we don't need the stethoscope anymore.
sentences.zh: 便携式超声波的兴起让一些医生认为我们不再需要听诊器了。

sentences.en: They say that if you have that technology, why not use it right away?
sentences.zh: 他们说，既然有这种技术，为什么不直接使用呢？

sentences.en: But ultrasound isn't available in many developing countries.
sentences.zh: 但在许多发展中国家，超声波设备并不普及。

sentences.en: And even in the United States, it's expensive.
sentences.zh: 即使在美国，它也很昂贵。

sentences.en: If we eliminated the stethoscope and everybody got an ultrasound at every visit,
sentences.zh: 如果我们淘汰了听诊器，让每个人每次就诊都做超声波检查，

sentences.en: we would bankrupt our healthcare system.
sentences.zh: 我们的医疗系统就会破产。

sentences.en: This is Dr. Dan Bernstein, a cardiologist at Stanford University.
sentences.zh: 这位是斯坦福大学的心脏病专家丹·伯恩斯坦医生。

sentences.en: He says that when he hears something problematic during the stethoscope exam,
sentences.zh: 他说，当他在听诊过程中听到异常情况时，

sentences.en: he immediately orders an ultrasound.
sentences.zh: 他会立即安排超声波检查。

sentences.en: But do I start with every patient who comes in the emergency room,
sentences.zh: 但我是否应该对每个走进急诊室的病人，

sentences.en: taking out the ultrasound machine, looking at the lungs?
sentences.zh: 都拿出超声波机器来检查肺部呢？

sentences.en: I think that's not a good use of that technology.
sentences.zh: 我认为那并不是对这项技术的合理利用。

sentences.en: Right now, he says the stethoscope functions as a screening tool,
sentences.zh: 他认为，目前听诊器起到了筛查工具的作用，

sentences.en: so that patients don't need to go get an expensive ultrasound unless they need one.
sentences.zh: 这样病人除非必要，否则无需进行昂贵的超声波检查。

sentences.en: Still, there's no denying that advanced imaging has changed the instrument's role.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，不可否认的是，先进的影像技术已经改变了听诊器的作用。

sentences.en: Dr. Andrew Baumbach says that medical students today
sentences.zh: 安德鲁·鲍姆巴赫医生表示，现在的医学生

sentences.en: aren't as good at listening to the body as they once were.
sentences.zh: 在听诊身体方面的能力不如从前了。

sentences.en: And across the board, doctors rely less on the stethoscope to make a diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 而且总的来说，医生在做出诊断时对听诊器的依赖程度也在降低。

sentences.en: It's become almost a ritual more than an actual tool of the trade
sentences.zh: 它已经变成了一种仪式，而不再是真正的专业工具，

sentences.en: in terms of helping us make diagnoses.
sentences.zh: 在辅助我们做出诊断方面（作用减弱）。

sentences.en: Recently, one of Dr. Baumbach's most respected colleagues asked to borrow a stethoscope.
sentences.zh: 最近，鲍姆巴赫医生最受尊敬的一位同事开口借用听诊器。

sentences.en: And Baumbach was embarrassed because the only one he had with him that day
sentences.zh: 鲍姆巴赫感到很尴尬，因为他那天随身携带的唯一一个，

sentences.en: was this cheap plastic disposable thing.
sentences.zh: 就是那种廉价的塑料一次性听诊器。

sentences.en: But he handed it over anyway.
sentences.zh: 但他还是递了过去。

sentences.en: And he said, oh yeah, thanks, that's perfect.
sentences.zh: 对方说，哦，好的，谢谢，这正合适。

sentences.en: And as he was walking away, he's like, you know,
sentences.zh: 当他走开时，他说，你知道吗，

sentences.en: patients just expect you to have this when you see them.
sentences.zh: 病人在看病时就是希望你身上有这个东西。

sentences.en: He's like, I'm not going to really need to use it.
sentences.zh: 他说，我其实并不需要真的用到它。

sentences.en: And I thought that was such a funny story because here's someone that I consider the consummate clinician.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这个故事很有趣，因为他是我心目中完美的临床医生。

sentences.en: And he was acknowledging that the stethoscope was in many ways just sort of a prop.
sentences.zh: 而他却承认听诊器在很多方面只是个道具。

sentences.en: But it's an omnipresent prop.
sentences.zh: 但它是一个无处不在的道具。

sentences.en: If you do a Google image search for doctor,
sentences.zh: 如果你在谷歌图片搜索“医生”，

sentences.en: right away you'll notice a couple of things about what a physician is supposed to look like.
sentences.zh: 你很快就会注意到关于医生形象的几个特点。

sentences.en: Most of the doctor's pictures on the first page of results are white men in white coats.
sentences.zh: 搜索结果第一页的大多数医生照片都是穿着白大褂的白人男性。

sentences.en: Some of them are peering inside a patient's ears.
sentences.zh: 有些人正在查看病人的耳朵。

sentences.en: Others are writing something down on a clipboard.
sentences.zh: 另一些人正在写字板上记录着什么。

sentences.en: But all of them have stethoscopes.
sentences.zh: 但他们所有人都戴着听诊器。

sentences.en: Well, what I find so intriguing about the Google images searches for doctor
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得谷歌图片搜索“医生”最耐人寻味的地方在于，

sentences.en: is not only is every doctor wearing a stethoscope,
sentences.zh: 不仅每个医生都戴着听诊器，

sentences.en: but they are almost all wearing the stethoscope in the exact same way,
sentences.zh: 而且他们几乎都是以完全相同的方式佩戴听诊器，

sentences.en: which is like a shawl around the back of the neck.
sentences.zh: 就像围巾一样挂在脖子后面。

sentences.en: With the earpieces on one side and the bell on the other.
sentences.zh: 耳塞在一侧，听诊头在另一侧。

sentences.en: Bombeck says that this way of wearing a stethoscope,
sentences.zh: 鲍姆巴赫说，这种佩戴听诊器的方式，

sentences.en: draped over the shoulders, is a relatively recent fashion trend.
sentences.zh: 即披在肩上，是一种相对较新的时尚潮流。

sentences.en: The first time I can remember ever seeing that was on the television show ER.
sentences.zh: 我记得第一次看到这种戴法是在电视剧《急诊室的故事》里。

sentences.en: And then on Scrubs, which is another very popular medical TV show.
sentences.zh: 后来又在另一部非常受欢迎的医疗剧《实习医生风云》中看到。

sentences.en: Doctors used to wear their stethoscopes dangling down the front of the shirt like a tie.
sentences.zh: 医生们过去常把听诊器像领带一样垂在衬衫前面。

sentences.en: And this was practical.
sentences.zh: 这很实用。

sentences.en: If you needed to use your stethoscope in a hurry,
sentences.zh: 如果你需要紧急使用听诊器，

sentences.en: you just popped it into your ears.
sentences.zh: 你只需把它塞进耳朵里就行了。

sentences.en: It's almost like this new version of wearing it like a scarf or a shawl
sentences.zh: 这种像围巾或披肩一样佩戴的新方式，

sentences.en: is almost a concession that it's more a fashion accessory
sentences.zh: 几乎承认了它更多是一种时尚配饰，

sentences.en: than actually a tool that we're using.
sentences.zh: 而不是我们真正使用的工具。

sentences.en: But even if the stethoscope exam has become something of a ritual,
sentences.zh: 但即使听诊检查已经变成了一种仪式，

sentences.en: it doesn't mean that doctors are ready to give it up.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着医生们准备放弃它。

sentences.en: I mean, I would never give up my stethoscope
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我永远不会放弃我的听诊器，

sentences.en: because I think in the very least,
sentences.zh: 因为我认为至少，

sentences.en: it's this conduit to connecting with a patient.
sentences.zh: 它是与病人建立联系的渠道。

sentences.en: Bomback says that physical contact between a doctor and a patient has become increasingly rare.
sentences.zh: 鲍姆巴赫说，医生和病人之间的身体接触已经变得越来越少。

sentences.en: Doctors' visits are short,
sentences.zh: 医生的问诊时间很短，

sentences.en: and physicians often spend half the time staring at a computer screen.
sentences.zh: 而且医生往往有一半的时间都在盯着电脑屏幕。

sentences.en: The stethoscope provides an important opportunity for intimacy.
sentences.zh: 听诊器提供了一个亲密接触的重要机会。

sentences.en: The stethoscope is still a part of the exam that is still very much aligned with that idea of the laying on of hands that a healer can do.
sentences.zh: 听诊器仍然是检查的一部分，它非常符合治疗者所能做的“按手礼”的理念。

sentences.en: When we go to do the physical exam, we move away from our desk,
sentences.zh: 当我们进行体格检查时，我们离开办公桌，

sentences.en: we move away from the computer, and we stand right next to the patient,
sentences.zh: 离开电脑，直接站在病人身边，

sentences.en: and it's a much more intimate conversation.
sentences.zh: 这是一种更加亲密的对话。

sentences.en: And even with all these powerful tools for measuring what's going on inside a body,
sentences.zh: 即使拥有了所有这些测量体内情况的强大工具，

sentences.en: intimate conversations are still really important in medicine.
sentences.zh: 亲密的对话在医学中仍然非常重要。

sentences.en: Dr. Bomback says he thinks that the stethoscope has come to symbolize to the patient
sentences.zh: 鲍姆巴赫医生说，他认为听诊器已经向病人传达了一个信号：

sentences.en: that the doctor is there to listen.
sentences.zh: 医生在这里倾听。

sentences.en: And whether we're actually listening to their heart or their lungs is probably not that important,
sentences.zh: 至于我们是否真的在听他们的心脏或肺部，可能并不那么重要，

sentences.en: but what they really want to know is that we're listening to what they say.
sentences.zh: 但他们真正想知道的是，我们在倾听他们所说的话。

sentences.en: 200 years ago, Rene Linek's invention ushered in a new medical era,
sentences.zh: 200年前，雷奈克的发明开启了一个新的医学时代，

sentences.en: one where the patient's own understanding of their disease
sentences.zh: 在这个时代，病人对自己疾病的理解，

sentences.en: gave way to more objective observation of the body.
sentences.zh: 让位于对身体更客观的观察。

sentences.en: This turn put a certain amount of distance between doctors and patients.
sentences.zh: 这种转变在医生和病人之间拉开了一定的距离。

sentences.en: Today, maybe the stethoscope lives on to keep physicians and patients from drifting too far apart,
sentences.zh: 今天，也许听诊器依然存在，是为了防止医生和病人走得太远，

sentences.en: to make sure doctors keep close to their patients, and keep listening.
sentences.zh: 确保医生与病人保持亲近，并继续倾听。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible will be back in a heartbeat after these messages.
sentences.zh: 《99%隐形》将在这些广告之后马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, it's Emmett.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是埃米特。

sentences.en: I'm back.
sentences.zh: 我回来了。

sentences.en: Okay, so real quick before we go.
sentences.zh: 好的，在我们结束之前快速说一下。

sentences.en: Remember when I mentioned that there are these new electronic stethoscopes?
sentences.zh: 还记得我提到过有这些新型电子听诊器吗？

sentences.en: Well, one is made by this company, Echo, which is based right here in Berkeley.
sentences.zh: 其中一款是由位于伯克利的Echo公司制造的。

sentences.en: And their stethoscope can record a patient's heartbeat, display the waveform,
sentences.zh: 他们的听诊器可以记录病人的心跳，显示波形，

sentences.en: and they're even working on software that can help doctors identify irregularities.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至正在开发可以帮助医生识别异常情况的软件。

sentences.en: I stopped by their offices and asked them to record my heart.
sentences.zh: 我去了他们的办公室，请他们记录我的心跳。

sentences.en: They pressed the device to my chest, and a little waveform popped up on a smartphone.
sentences.zh: 他们把设备按在我的胸口，智能手机上就弹出了一个小波形。

sentences.en: At the top here, you see the heart start to fire.
sentences.zh: 在这里的顶部，你可以看到心脏开始跳动。

sentences.en: You actually see that's called the P-wave right there.
sentences.zh: 你实际上看到的那就是所谓的P波。

sentences.en: That's Echo founder Connor Landgraf.
sentences.zh: 那是Echo的创始人康纳·兰格拉夫。

sentences.en: And while he is not a doctor, he says my heart looks healthy.
sentences.zh: 虽然他不是医生，但他表示我的心脏看起来很健康。

sentences.en: Pretty normal-looking waveform.
sentences.zh: 波形看起来很正常。

sentences.en: Nothing really interesting looking there, unfortunately.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，看起来没什么特别有趣的。

sentences.en: Fortunately.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是。

sentences.en: Yeah, I guess fortunately for you, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我想对你来说是幸运的，没错。

sentences.en: So just to send us off, here's my unfortunate heartbeat.
sentences.zh: 所以最后，这是我那“不幸”的心跳声。

sentences.en: Well, Emmett, you have a very disappointingly boring heartbeat.
sentences.zh: 好吧，埃米特，你的心跳真是令人失望地无聊。

sentences.en: Sorry, boss.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，老板。

sentences.zh: 德莱尼·霍尔和谢里夫·优素福提供了制作协助。

sentences.zh: 我们的高级制作人是凯蒂·明格尔。

sentences.zh: 音乐由肖恩·里亚尔创作。

sentences.zh: 其他工作人员包括艾弗里·特鲁夫曼、塔琳·马扎，以及我，罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.zh: 特别感谢安娜·普拉格，她激发了我们的这个灵感。

sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山91.7 KALW的一个项目，在加利福尼亚州美丽的奥克兰市中心Radio Row制作。

sentences.zh: 由“捍卫新闻基金会”和像你一样自掏腰包的听众支持。

sentences.zh: 你可以在Facebook上找到我们的节目并参与讨论。

sentences.zh: 你可以在推特上关注我@RomanMars，以及节目@99pi.org。

sentences.zh: 我们也在Instagram、Tumblr和Reddit上。

sentences.zh: 但你可以在我们的网站99pi.org上找到所有往期节目，以及每周至少两篇关于设计的文章。
